title: Find the shift signal
brief:
Your QI team has been working since March on improving the proportion of children under five with a malaria-positive RDT who are dispensed an artemisinin-based combination therapy (ACT) **on the same day** at a rural health centre. The chart below shows the last 20 weeks of weekly data.

Using Provost & Murray’s **shift rule** — six or more consecutive points on one side of the median signal a non-random change — click the points that make up the shift.

(Tip: keyboard users can press Tab to enter the chart, then Left/Right arrow to move between points, and Enter to select.)

exhibit.title: Same-day ACT dispensing for malaria-positive children U5 (weekly)

task.stem: Click each point that is part of the shift (the run of consecutive points entirely on one side of the median). Submit when you have the full shift selected.

debrief.correct: Spotted. Weeks 9–15 are all above the median (65%) — that is **seven** consecutive points above, which exceeds the threshold of six for the shift rule. The drop after week 15 is back into routine variation. A shift is one of the four classic run-chart signals; the others are trend, runs (too many / too few crossings of the median), and astronomical point.
debrief.wrong: The shift rule: **six or more consecutive points entirely on one side of the median** (points on the median do not count). Look for the run starting around week 9 — seven points are above the median (65%) before the chart drops back. The eye is often drawn to the peak (week 14, 76%), but the signal is the sustained run, not the maximum.
debrief.rule_cited: Provost & Murray (2nd ed.) — Shift rule (≥ 6 consecutive points on one side of the median).
